content.text:
I reviewed the brief line by line against the 8-K Exhibit 99.1. Summary of what I found:

**Headline numbers** (sales, GAAP and adjusted EPS, net earnings, free cash flow, both guidance raises, segment and regional growth rates) all tie to the release, including basis labels.

**Two problems:**
1. **"TECVAYLI + DARZALEX FASPRO (multiple myeloma)"** — the release's data highlight is **TALVEY** plus DARZALEX FASPRO. TECVAYLI appears separately (plus daratumumab, CHMP recommendation; and its own PFS/OS data). The combination as the brief names it is not in the release.
2. **"Dual Energy THERMOCOOL SMARTTOUCH SF (cardiology platform)"** — the release never characterizes it as a cardiology platform, and the approval item carries footnote 1, "subsequent to the quarter."

**Notable omissions:** the STELARA ~760 bps drag on Innovative Medicine operational growth is nowhere in the brief (nor REMICADE/ZYTIGA among the offsets), and the segment dollar sales ($16,384M / $8,926M) are not given, only the growth rates. The brief also attributes the Innovative Medicine driver list to 7.8% *reported* growth, whereas the release's commentary is framed on 6.8% *operational*.

**Watch Items** contains two assertions that go beyond the release: that guidance "assumes continued success in TECVAYLI, RYBREVANT, and IMAAVY," and that the absence of GAAP guidance "suggests volatility" — the release says only that it cannot predict those items with reasonable certainty.

facts.evidence: Reported sales of **$25.3 billion** in Q2 2026, up **6.6%** year-over-year
Reported earnings per share (EPS) of **$2.27**, down **0.9%** from $2.29 in Q2 2025
**adjusted EPS** rose **4.7%** to **$2.90** (excluding intangible amortization and special items)
**Innovative Medicine** delivered **7.8% reported sales growth** (the $16,384 million sales figure and the comparison to MedTech as the larger segment are not given)
**adjusted EPS** guidance increased by **$0.13** to **$11.68** (midpoint, **8.2% growth**)
The company raised **2026 full-year guidance**, with **reported sales** now expected to reach **$101.1 billion** (midpoint, **7.3% growth**)
Free cash flow for Q2 2026 (year-to-date) was approximately **$8.7 billion**, up from **$6.2 billion** in Q2 2025.

**MedTech** grew **4.5%**, led by **wound closure, biosurgery (Surgery), electrophysiology, Shockwave (Cardiovascular), contact lenses (Vision), and trauma (Orthopaedics)** (the $8,926 million sales figure is not given)
with **operational sales growth of 5.6%** and **adjusted operational sales growth of 5.7%**

claims.claim: Reported sales were $25.3 billion in Q2 2026, up 6.6% year-over-year.
Q2 2026 operational sales growth was 5.6%.
Q2 2026 adjusted operational sales growth was 5.7%.
Reported (diluted) EPS was $2.27, down 0.9% from $2.29 in Q2 2025.
Adjusted EPS rose 4.7% to $2.90.
Adjusted EPS excludes intangible amortization and special items.
Free cash flow for Q2 2026 year-to-date was approximately $8.7 billion, up from $6.2 billion in the prior-year period.
Net earnings were $5.5 billion in Q2 2026, down 0.1% year-over-year.
The company raised its 2026 full-year guidance.
2026 estimated reported sales guidance is $101.1 billion at the midpoint, 7.3% growth.
2026 adjusted EPS guidance was increased by $0.13 to $11.68 at the midpoint, 8.2% growth.
Innovative Medicine delivered 7.8% reported sales growth.
Innovative Medicine growth was driven by DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, TECVAYLI and RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE in Oncology, TREMFYA in Immunology, and SPRAVATO and CAPLYTA in Neuroscience.
claims.note: Driver list matches the release, though the release frames these as drivers of 6.8% operational growth, not the 7.8% reported growth the brief cites.

claims.claim: Innovative Medicine growth was partially offset by STELARA and IMBRUVICA.
MedTech grew 4.5%.
MedTech growth was led by wound closure and biosurgery products in Surgery, electrophysiology products and Shockwave in Cardiovascular, contact lenses in Vision, and trauma in Orthopaedics.
U.S. sales rose 7.3% on an operational basis.
International sales grew 5.7% on a reported basis.
U.S. adjusted operational growth was 7.4%.
International adjusted operational growth was 3.5%.
TREMFYA received approval to inhibit progression of structural joint damage in active psoriatic arthritis.
CAPLYTA received approval for prevention of relapse in schizophrenia.
The Dual Energy THERMOCOOL SMARTTOUCH SF cardiology platform was among the quarter's key regulatory approvals.
claims.note: The release never describes the platform as a cardiology platform (outside knowledge), and the FDA approval item carries footnote 1, 'Subsequent to the quarter,' so presenting it among in-quarter approvals is not supported.

claims.claim: 2026 guidance projects operational sales of $100.6 billion at the midpoint, 6.8% growth.
2026 guidance projects adjusted operational EPS of $11.58 at the midpoint, 7.3% growth.
No GAAP guidance was provided for 2026 because of uncertainty over legal proceedings, acquisitions and special items.
Pipeline advancements include RYBREVANT FASPRO data in head and neck cancer.
Pipeline advancements include TECVAYLI plus DARZALEX FASPRO in multiple myeloma.
claims.note: The release's highlighted data are for TALVEY plus DARZALEX FASPRO in earlier-line relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; TECVAYLI appears separately (plus daratumumab in a CHMP recommendation, and standalone PFS/OS data). The combination as named is not in the release.

claims.claim: Pipeline advancements include OTTAVA in upper abdominal procedures.
The release provides no specific debt or capital allocation details.
Recent investments include more than $1 billion in U.S. vision manufacturing.
Recent investments include the acquisition of Firefly Bio to expand the oncology pipeline.
claims.note: Release states J&J is 'to Acquire' Firefly Bio, i.e. announced rather than completed; substance otherwise matches.

claims.claim: The company's guidance assumes continued success in TECVAYLI, RYBREVANT and IMAAVY.
claims.note: The release states no product-level assumptions underlying guidance; this is the analyst's inference.

claims.claim: International adjusted operational growth of 3.5% lags U.S. adjusted operational growth of 7.4%.
The absence of GAAP guidance suggests volatility in legal, acquisition or special-item costs.
claims.note: The release attributes the omission to an inability to predict these items with reasonable certainty without unreasonable effort; it does not assert volatility in those costs.
